paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and Paul calls that "a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance" (1 Timothy 1:15). Then he says he is the worst of them. Paul was a blasphemer, a persecutor and a violent man, and Jesus still showed him mercy, and "the grace of our Lord overflowed" to him (1 Timothy 1:13-14). If that was enough for Paul, there's no pile of past too big for it, and that includes yours.

Why did Jesus do that? Paul says it was so "Christ Jesus might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life" (1 Timothy 1:16). Paul's story is a sign saying, "Look, He does this for people who believe." That should make you want to do what Paul does and burst into praise: "Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen." (1 Timothy 1:17)

Mercy doesn't mean you can stop paying attention, though. Paul tells Timothy, his child in the faith, to fight the good fight by "holding on to faith and a good conscience," which some have rejected and so shipwrecked their faith (1 Timothy 1:18-19). So take the mercy Paul got, hold on tight, and don't let go. I know a thing or two about being picked up when I thought I was done for, and I'm not letting go either.
